title: Article 329 — Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters

content.overview: Article 329 bars courts from interfering in certain electoral matters. Notwithstanding anything in the Constitution, the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies, made or purporting to be made under Article 327 or 328, shall not be called in question in any court. No election to either House of Parliament or to the House or either House of a State Legislature shall be called in question except by an election petition presented to such authority and in such manner as may be provided by or under any law made by the appropriate Legislature.
content.glance: Delimitation/seat-allotment laws under Arts 327–328 not open to court challenge. Election challenge only by election petition before the authority and in the manner provided by law.
content.study:
Article 329 electoral bar:
**(a)** Validity of delimitation or seat-allotment law under Art 327 or 328 shall not be called in question in any court.
**(b)** No election to Parliament or a State Legislature shall be called in question except by an election petition presented to such authority and in such manner as provided by or under law of the appropriate Legislature.

Election petitions under the Representation of the People Act are the exclusive remedy for challenging elections. The bar does not oust all judicial review in every context (e.g. pre-election process issues have been treated carefully in case law), but the constitutional design channels post-election challenges into the statutory election-petition route.

Examination: delimitation immunity; exclusive election-petition remedy; appropriate Legislature’s law; contrast Art 324 plenary power.

sections.heading: Two bars
sections.body:
1. Delimitation / seat-allotment laws under Arts 327–328: not open to question in any court.
2. Elections to Parliament / State Legislature: challenge only by election petition before the prescribed authority in the prescribed manner.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the bar under Article 329.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 329 provides that the validity of any law relating to the delimitation of constituencies or the allotment of seats to such constituencies, made or purporting to be made under Article 327 or Article 328, shall not be called in question in any court. It further provides that no election to either House of Parliament or to the House or either House of the Legislature of a State shall be called in question except by an election petition presented to such authority and in such manner as may be provided by or under any law made by the appropriate Legislature.

examTips: Delimitation not justiciable; election challenge only by election petition.

keyTakeaways: Art 329: bar on court interference — delimitation immunity; election petition exclusive.
